utilities.population: boys aged 1-12 years with severe hemophilia A without FVIII inhibitors
utilities.description: Common utility parameters are used for both strategies. Treatment-specific QALY differences arise only through different simulated clinical histories (bleeding, Pettersson progression, ICH sequelae, and death).

baseline_pediatric_utility.interpretation: 0.952 is not a directly observed PS=0 utility and is not a treatment-specific prophylaxis benefit. It is used as a common pediatric absolute utility anchor.

reference.citation: Zhang L, Zhang P, Chen W. Treatment regimens, patient reported outcomes and health-related quality of life in children with moderate and severe hemophilia A in China: using real-world data. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2023;18:232. doi:10.1186/s13023-023-02835-x.
reference.population: 373 boys aged <=18 years with moderate or severe hemophilia A without FVIII inhibitors; mean age 7.3 years; 69.7% severe.
limitations: The source group contained both moderate and severe hemophilia A.
The source group was treatment-defined, not Pettersson-defined.
Mean annual bleeds were 9.8 and mean target joints were 0.3; therefore the value is not interpreted as perfect health or PS=0.

psa.uncertainty_target: sampling uncertainty in the source-group mean

reference.citation: Fischer K, de Kleijn P, Negrier C, et al. The association of haemophilic arthropathy with Health-Related Quality of Life: a post hoc analysis. Haemophilia. 2016;22(6):833-840. doi:10.1111/hae.13120.
reference.population: 176 assessments in 159 patients with moderate/severe hemophilia A or B; minimum age 16 years; median age 26.6 years; 89.9% severe; 84.7% hemophilia A.
reference.key_interpretation: Observed mean utility declined from 0.80 in PS 0-4 and 5-12 to 0.77 in PS 13-21 and 0.70 in PS 22-39. The 0.03 decrement at PS 13-21 was below the reported SF-6D MID of 0.041 and was not statistically significant; significant deterioration was concentrated above PS 21. No additional significant decline was observed for PS 40-78.

ps_40_78.note: The slightly higher mean than PS 22-39 is not allowed to create increasing utility with worsening arthropathy.

chronic_arthropathy_utility_mapping.base_case_principle: Use the observed Fischer relative utility pattern rather than adult absolute SF-6D values. The PS 13-21 observed mean effect is retained in the base case despite being below the MID; a threshold-based no-decrement alternative is tested structurally.

threshold_based_no_mild_decrement.description: Reflect Fischer's finding that significant deterioration was concentrated above PS 21.

direct_absolute_fischer_mapping.description: Use adult Fischer SF-6D utilities directly to test the pediatric anchoring assumption.

reference.citation: Neufeld EJ, Recht M, Sabio H, et al. Effect of acute bleeding on daily quality of life assessments in patients with congenital hemophilia with inhibitors and their families. Value Health. 2012;15(6):916-925. doi:10.1016/j.jval.2012.05.005.
reference.overall_evidence: Mean EQ-5D index 0.66 on bleed days versus 0.82 on nonbleed days; difference 0.16.
reference.pediatric_support: Patient-mean EQ-5D in age <=18 years was 0.76 on bleed days versus 0.92 on nonbleed days; difference 0.16.
reference.bleed_type_support: Joint and other bleed types showed comparable acute QOL deviations in the study.
reference.population_limitation: Congenital hemophilia with inhibitors; used as indirect daily bleed-effect evidence for inhibitor-negative severe HA.

psa.note: The +/-20% range is not a reported CI or SD.

psa.uncertainty_target: mean acute-burden duration per minor bleed

duration_days.interpretation: The same base-case acute duration is used for joint and non-major non-joint bleeds because direct comparative utility-duration evidence is lacking. Joint bleeds remain distinct because each joint bleed updates cumulative joint-bleed history and future Pettersson progression.

duration_evidence.citation: Manco-Johnson MJ, et al. Prophylaxis versus Episodic Treatment to Prevent Joint Disease in Boys with Severe Hemophilia. N Engl J Med. 2007;357:535-544. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa067659.
duration_evidence.evidence: Enhanced episodic treatment of hemarthrosis included dosing at recognition, 24 h and 72 h, with continued every-other-day dosing permitted until pain and impaired mobility resolved.

duration_evidence.citation: Gringeri A, et al. A randomized clinical trial of prophylaxis in children with hemophilia A (the ESPRIT Study). J Thromb Haemost. 2011;9:700-710. doi:10.1111/j.1538-7836.2011.04214.x.
duration_evidence.evidence: Children aged 1-7 years on episodic therapy received FVIII every 12-24 h until complete clinical bleeding resolution.

duration_evidence.citation: Young G, et al. Recombinant factor VIII Fc fusion protein for the prevention and treatment of bleeding in children with severe hemophilia A. J Thromb Haemost. 2015;13:967-977. doi:10.1111/jth.12911.
duration_evidence.evidence: In children <12 years with severe HA, 93% of bleeding episodes were controlled with one or two rFVIIIFc infusions.

differential_duration.purpose: Tests the possibility that joint bleeds have longer acute burden than non-joint minor bleeds.

long_term_state_update.pettersson_update: Apply the separate model rule linking cumulative joint bleeds to Pettersson score.

reference.citation: Cook K, Forbes SP, Adamski K, Ma JJ, Chawla A, Garrison LP Jr. Assessing the potential cost-effectiveness of a gene therapy for the treatment of hemophilia A. J Med Econ. 2020;23(5):501-512. doi:10.1080/13696998.2020.1721508.

alternative_published_model_scenario.reason_not_base_case: May overlap with separately modeled chronic Pettersson-mediated joint burden.

non_ich_major_bleeding.scope: major extracranial bleeding; base-case proxy is nonfatal GI bleeding

reference.citation: Hogg K, Kimpton M, Carrier M, Coyle D, Forgie M, Wells P. Estimating Quality of Life in Acute Venous Thrombosis. JAMA Intern Med. 2013;173(12):1067-1072. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.563.
reference.duration_basis_in_source: expert consensus for bleeding health states
reference.population_limitation: Adult thrombosis-clinic population; not pediatric and not hemophilia-specific.

psa.note: IQR endpoints are not empirical minimum and maximum.

psa.uncertainty_type: pragmatic modeling range around Hogg's 1-week health-state duration

clinical_reference.citation: Srivastava A, Santagostino E, Dougall A, et al. WFH Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia, 3rd edition. Haemophilia. 2020;26(Suppl 6):1-158. doi:10.1111/hae.14046.
clinical_reference.relevance: WFH states that treatment amount and duration depend on bleed site/severity; GI and throat/neck bleeds require continued hemostatic coverage until bleeding/symptoms resolve.

reference.citation: Hogg K, Kimpton M, Carrier M, Coyle D, Forgie M, Wells P. Estimating Quality of Life in Acute Venous Thrombosis. JAMA Intern Med. 2013;173(12):1067-1072. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.563.
reference.population_limitation: Adult thrombosis-clinic population; not pediatric and not hemophilia-specific.
reference.modeling_interpretation: Used only as a proxy for acute ICH severity; persistent consequences are modeled separately.

psa.note: IQR endpoints are not empirical minimum and maximum.

psa.uncertainty_target: mean duration of the acute ICH phase
psa.uncertainty_type: evidence-informed proxy based on hemostatic treatment duration

reference.citation: Srivastava A, Santagostino E, Dougall A, et al. WFH Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia, 3rd edition. Haemophilia. 2020;26(Suppl 6):1-158. doi:10.1111/hae.14046.
reference.evidence: For confirmed CNS bleeding, WFH recommends maintaining appropriate factor levels for 10-14 days.
reference.limitation: This is a treatment-duration recommendation, used as a proxy for the acute utility-duration window.

post_ich_outcomes.trigger: Evaluate only for survivors of ICH after the acute ICH phase.

reference.citation: Sezgin Evim M, et al. Risk factors for neurologic sequelae in children and adolescents with hemophilia after intracranial hemorrhage. Res Pract Thromb Haemost. 2024;8(8):102607. doi:10.1016/j.rpth.2024.102607.
reference.population: Children and adolescents with hemophilia and ICH.
reference.derivation: 18 neurologic sequelae among 70 survivors whose ICH occurred after the newborn period.
reference.reason_for_subset: The microsimulation begins at age 1 year.

psa.uncertainty_target: binomial proportion based on observed counts

persistent_neurologic_sequelae.definition_warning: The Sezgin Evim outcome is any persistent neurologic sequela and is not identical to mRS 3-5 disability.

reference.citation: Glaeser-Khan S, Ito S, Sra M, et al. Emicizumab for preventing intracranial hemorrhage in infants with severe hemophilia A: a cost-effectiveness analysis. Blood Adv. 2025;9(24):6237-6245. doi:10.1182/bloodadvances.2025016822.
reference.source_definition: Published model utility for disability after ICH, mRS 3-5.

utility_if_persistent_sequela.limitation: Mapping all Sezgin Evim persistent sequelae to the mRS 3-5 utility is not directly observed and may overstate the severity of some sequelae.

survivor_without_persistent_sequela.base_case_rule: Return to the pre-ICH chronic arthropathy utility after the acute ICH phase.
survivor_without_persistent_sequela.rationale: Avoids an unsupported permanent penalty when no persistent neurologic sequela is recorded.

less_severe_mapping_for_recorded_sequela.description: Apply the Glaeser-Khan no/mild-disability utility cap to recorded sequelae as an upper-bound scenario.

reference.citation: Glaeser-Khan S, Ito S, Sra M, et al. Blood Adv. 2025;9(24):6237-6245. doi:10.1182/bloodadvances.2025016822.
reference.source_definition: Utility for no/mild disability after ICH, mRS 0-2.

published_glaeser_khan_two_state_structu.description: Use the published hemophilia ICH economic-model structure as a package.

reference.citation: Glaeser-Khan S, Ito S, Sra M, et al. Blood Adv. 2025;9(24):6237-6245. doi:10.1182/bloodadvances.2025016822.

published_glaeser_khan_two_state_structu.limitation: The published model targets infants aged 0-1 year, whereas the present microsimulation starts at age 1 year.

event_order: evaluate ICH case fatality at the event time
if fatal: transition to death and do not evaluate sequelae
if survived: initialize acute_ich_time_remaining_days and apply acute ICH utility cap
after acute ICH phase: if no pre-existing sequela flag, sample persistent neurologic sequelae
if sequela occurs: set post_ich_neurologic_sequelae_flag=true permanently
implementation.recurrent_ich_rule: If the sequela flag is already true, it remains true after subsequent nonfatal ICH. If false, sequelae may be evaluated after each survived ICH.

within_cycle_onset.rule: Assign each acute event an onset time within the weekly cycle.
within_cycle_onset.recommended_sampling: Uniform over the 7-day cycle when no empirical day-of-week pattern is modeled.
within_cycle_onset.purpose: Allows duration to cross cycle boundaries and avoids forcing every event to start at the cycle boundary.

carryover.rule: Any unused event duration at cycle end is carried into subsequent cycles.

overlap.rule: At any time point, calculate all applicable event utilities and use the lowest resulting utility.
overlap.joint_history_rule: Each joint bleed increments cumulative joint-bleed history even if its acute utility interval overlaps another event.

acute_event_timing_and_overlap.death: Truncate all active event durations at death.

weekly_qaly_calculation.reason_for_364: The model defines one weekly cycle as 1/52 of a model year. Therefore 7 model-days correspond to 1/52 year, and daily utility weights are 1/(52*7)=1/364. Using 365.25 while also using exactly 52 cycles/year would under-accrue QALYs.
weekly_qaly_calculation.step_1: Determine U_arthropathy from current Pettersson score.
weekly_qaly_calculation.step_2: Apply permanent post-ICH utility cap if the sequela flag is active.
weekly_qaly_calculation.step_3: Apply acute-event decrement/cap over the fraction of the cycle affected by each event.
weekly_qaly_calculation.general_formula: weekly_QALY = integral_over_cycle(U(t) dt) / 364, with t measured in model-days
weekly_qaly_calculation.partial_day_rule: If a sampled duration is fractional, weight the final affected day by the corresponding fractional day.

death_rule.within_cycle: Accrue QALY only for time alive before death.

zhang_2023.reference: Zhang L, Zhang P, Chen W. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2023;18:232. doi:10.1186/s13023-023-02835-x.
zhang_2023.use: Face-validity check for overall simulated utilities; treatment-group values must not be assigned directly to model arms.
zhang_2023.independence_note: The long-term prophylaxis value is also used as the common pediatric anchor, so it is not an independent validation of that anchor.

neufeld_2012_pediatric_diary.reference: Neufeld EJ, Recht M, Sabio H, et al. Value Health. 2012;15(6):916-925. doi:10.1016/j.jval.2012.05.005.
neufeld_2012_pediatric_diary.use: External plausibility check for high pediatric nonbleed utility and for the approximately 0.16 acute bleed decrement.
neufeld_2012_pediatric_diary.limitation: Patients had congenital hemophilia with inhibitors and frequent bleeding.

wasserman_2005.reference: Wasserman J, Aday LA, Begley CE, Ahn C, Lairson DR. Measuring health state preferences for hemophilia: development of a disease-specific utility instrument. Haemophilia. 2005;11(1):49-57. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2516.2005.01054.x.
wasserman_2005.use: External validation only; the vignettes describe a hypothetical 21-year-old and already embed treatment, bleeding, and joint consequences.
